sources.note: Only first-hand Punan Aput material known: consultant Yuriana Long of Long Sule (p. 16 = PDF p. 46); sec. 2.4 Punan pp. 111-127 gives PMP > Punan sound correspondences (tables 29-31), Punan-internal subgrouping and the vowel system ('All other Punan dialects have a standard six vowel system, with i, e, a, o, u, and schwa', p. 126); Appendix 3 Punan comparative wordlist pp. 491-515 has a Punan Aput row with no stress marks; sec. 4.3.4.3 p. 404 is oral history. No statement about word stress in any Punan dialect (the dissertation's stress remarks concern Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh and…

sources.citation: Guerreiro, Antonio J. 1996. Homophony, sound changes and dialectal variations in some central Bornean languages. Mon-Khmer Studies 25: 205-226.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kayanic (Kayan, Modang, Bahau) sound changes; Punan Aput is not a subject language. 'Punan' appears only where a Modang /c/ is suggested to be a loan from the Punan of the upper Kelai (p. 209; that is Punan Kelai, a Segai-Modang group). The sole stress-related line is Haudricourt's general remark that 'unstressed vowels /e/ are dropped' on the road to monosyllabism in Modang (p. 212). Silent on Punan Aput.
No phonology; cite only Ethnologue and Glottolog.
